subtitle: Monthly horror picks for the mortally curious.

novels.title: Blood Meridian
novels.author: Cormac McCarthy (1985)
novels.vibe: A brutal, biblical Western that reads as horror through sheer unrelenting violence and nihilism.
novels.summary: A teenage runaway known only as "the kid" falls in with the Glanton gang, a real historical group of scalp hunters terrorizing the Texas-Mexico borderlands in the 1840s. The novel follows their atrocities in stark, unpunctuated prose, centered on the enigmatic, seemingly immortal Judge Holden.
novels.warnings: Extreme graphic violence, genocide, racism, child endangerment and death, sexual violence (referenced), animal death.

novels.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes
novels.author: Ray Bradbury (1962)
novels.vibe: A lyrical, autumnal dark-carnival classic about two boys and the sinister traveling show that arrives in their small town.
novels.summary: Best friends Will and Jim are captivated by a mysterious carnival that rolls into their Midwestern town in the dead of night, offering townsfolk their secret desires at a terrible cost. A carousel that ages riders forward or backward becomes the centerpiece of a story about temptation, mortality, and the pull of adulthood.
novels.warnings: Body horror (aging/transformation), period-typical sexism, mild violence, thematic dread rather than graphic content.

novels.title: The Exorcist
novels.author: William Peter Blatty (1971)
novels.vibe: The classic possession novel that defined the genre — a mother's search for answers as her daughter's body and mind are taken over by something ancient.
novels.summary: When young Regan begins exhibiting terrifying, inexplicable behavior, her mother exhausts every medical explanation before turning to the Church for help. Two priests are drawn into a brutal, escalating exorcism that tests their faith as much as it endangers their lives, in the novel that inspired the landmark film.
novels.warnings: Graphic violence against a child, blasphemy/religious desecration, disturbing sexual content, profanity, body horror.

novels.title: The Haunting of Hill House
novels.author: Shirley Jackson (1959)
novels.vibe: The gothic haunted-house novel every other haunted-house novel is quietly arguing with, built on dread rather than gore.
novels.summary: Four seekers, including a scholar of the paranormal and the fragile, lonely Eleanor, take up residence in Hill House to study its reputed hauntings. The house's influence grows increasingly personal and psychological rather than overtly supernatural, tightening around Eleanor in particular as the group's grip on reality frays.
novels.warnings: Suicide (by hanging and by car collision), suicidal ideation, mental illness/psychosis, gaslighting, death of a parent (off-page).

short_works.title: The Lottery
short_works.author: Shirley Jackson (1948)
short_works.vibe: The quiet-town-with-a-terrible-secret story that basically invented the genre — banal ritual violence played completely straight.
short_works.summary: Every year, the residents of a small American town gather for an annual lottery, presented at first as an unremarkable civic tradition. As the ritual unfolds, the story reveals exactly what "winning" the lottery means, and how easily ordinary people participate in cruelty when it's sanctioned by custom.

short_works.title: The Husband Stitch
short_works.author: Carmen Maria Machado (2014)
short_works.vibe: A feminist body-horror fairy tale about a woman, her husband, and the one thing she asks him never to touch.
short_works.summary: A woman narrates her life and marriage, folk-tale style, centered on a green ribbon tied around her neck that her husband is never permitted to touch. Interweaving classic ghost-story tropes with a story about bodily autonomy and consent, it builds to the ribbon's inevitable, devastating unraveling.
short_works.warnings: Sexual content and sexual abuse, body horror, medical content/childbirth, domestic abuse, brief cannibalism reference.

short_works.title: Where Are You Going, Where Have You Been?
short_works.author: Joyce Carol Oates (1966)
short_works.vibe: A slow-dread psychological horror classic about a teenage girl and the predatory stranger who shows up at her door.
short_works.summary: Fifteen-year-old Connie, home alone while her family is out, is approached by a charming but increasingly unsettling older man who seems to know far more about her than he should. Inspired by a real serial killer, the story builds an atmosphere of mounting menace entirely through dialogue and implication.
short_works.warnings: Sexual predation/grooming of a minor, psychological threat and coercion, implied violence.
